candidates.seed: St Monica's church, Edgware Road, at night: a narrow Victorian chapel built as a ONE-WALL CUTAWAY diorama, the south wall removed so the viewer looks straight into the nave from outside. WIDE LANDSCAPE FRAME. The chancel and the altar stand at the RIGHT-HAND end and the nave runs away down and to the LEFT. The standing north wall is warm cream plaster with a scatter of exposed stone courses, and it carries TWO tall narrow gothic lancet windows whose glass is the coolest brightest thing in the picture, glowing pale moonlit blue-white. The east wall behind the altar carries ONE big three-light gothic window with stone tracery, rising past the eaves into the gable, its glass a deeper slate blue. The chancel is raised one step and is lit warm AMBER by a pair of tall lit altar candles, while the nave beyond stays cool and moonlit -- the warm light and the cool light never mix. On the altar: a cream cloth, an open book, a brass candlestick pair with lit candles, a small brass HOURGLASS with amber sand, and one deep crimson flower bloom. A low dark wooden altar rail with turned balusters runs across the front of the chancel. Rows of near-black pews fill the nave, each with a warm amber lit top rail. A crimson runner runs down the centre aisle and up the chancel step. THREE faceted figures stand in a knot in front of the altar: a clergyman in a white surplice, a bride in a cream dress and veil, and a groom in a dark coat. Open dark timber roof trusses and a ridge beam above. The chapel is a compact narrow building with deliberately oversized figures inside it -- the eaves sit only about one and a half figure heights above the floor. The whole diorama sits CENTRED with clear empty dark void at both the left and the right edge of the frame, and dark void above the roof ridge.
